title: Fact hydration
preamble:
# Fact hydration

On-demand loading of
historical data as facts: a rule issues an async call to
an adapter that holds history; the adapter asserts
matching records back into the engine's working memory as
facts of the requested schema, bounded by a correlation id
and an explicit TTL.

Paired with:
- [LSTO] — the facts and samples planes
  hydration reads from.
- [LCRS] — the call/response
  machinery hydration calls build on (async dispatch,
  correlation, `CallError`).
- [LSER] — hydrated facts interact with
  series (hydrated-facts-don't-feed-series rule below).
- [LFAC] — lifecycle semantics.

## What this is not

- Not a subscription model — every hydration is
  explicitly requested; nothing continuous.
- Not `cached(...)` — cache is sync-intent KV
  current-state; hydration is async multi-fact historical
  load.
- Not a replacement for live facts — hydration is a
  snapshot at query time.
- Not a grammar for arbitrary backend queries — caller
  specifies schema + simple predicate + window.
- Not an implementation spec — see
  [RHIM].
